title: Custom homes
summary: Ground-up coastal homes, from first budget to final walkthrough, with design-build available.
intro: We build custom homes in Newport Beach and coastal Orange County, and we pour the foundation and frame the structure with our own crews. Design-build is available, so a single team can carry a home from early budgeting through construction.

heroImage.alt: Placeholder standing in for a finished exterior photo of 4 Fairway Point, Newport Coast

included.title: General construction
included.body: One general contractor responsible for the whole build, from site work to finishes.

included.title: Design-build
included.body: Design and construction under one contract, so budget and buildability are part of the design conversation from the start.

included.title: Structural concrete
included.body: Footings, slabs and structural concrete placed by our own crew.

included.title: Rough framing
included.body: Our framing crew builds the structure, including pre-fab and modular framing where it fits the project.

included.title: Soft/hardscape, pools and spas
included.body: Outdoor living built as part of the same contract as the house.

included.title: Quantity take-offs and budgets
included.body: Line-item quantities and budgets before you commit, revisited as the design develops.

process.title: Budget
process.body: We build a working budget from your goals, the lot and early plans, using quantity take-offs rather than square-foot guesses.

process.title: Design
process.body: With your architect, or through design-build, we review plans for cost and constructability as they develop.

process.title: Permit
process.body: We help assemble and track the permit submittal and respond to plan-check comments.

process.title: Build
process.body: We pour, frame and manage every trade through completion, with weekly meetings and job documentation.

faqs.question: Do you pour and frame the house yourselves?
faqs.answer: Yes. We self-perform structural concrete and rough framing, so the bones of the house are built by our own crews rather than subcontracted.

faqs.question: Do you offer design-build?
faqs.answer: Yes. Design-build is one of our services, and we also build from plans prepared by your own architect.

faqs.question: Can you build the pool and landscape too?
faqs.answer: Yes. Soft and hardscape, pools and spas are part of what we build.

faqs.question: How long does a custom home take to build?
Where do you build?
faqs.answer: Newport Beach and coastal Orange County, including Newport Coast, Corona del Mar, Costa Mesa and Huntington Beach.

title: Remodels & additions
summary: Remodels and additions that tie new structure cleanly into an existing home.
intro: Remodels and additions are where structure matters most: new work has to meet old work cleanly. Because we do our own concrete and framing, the structural side of a remodel stays with the same team that manages the rest of the job.

heroImage.alt: Placeholder standing in for a finished exterior photo of 1418 Balboa Blvd, Newport Beach

included.title: Remodels
included.body: Interior and whole-house remodels managed by one general contractor.

included.title: Additions
included.body: New foundations and framing tied into the existing structure by our own crews.

included.title: Plan review
included.body: We review plans for cost and constructability before pricing, so surprises surface on paper first.

included.title: Budgets and change orders
included.body: A clear budget up front, and documented change orders if the scope moves.

process.title: Budget
process.body: We walk the house with you and price the work from plans and quantities.

process.title: Design
process.body: We review drawings with your designer or architect for cost and buildability.

process.title: Permit
process.body: We help prepare the permit submittal and work through plan-check comments.

process.title: Build
process.body: We build, keep you updated in weekly meetings and document the job as it goes.

faqs.question: Do you take on remodels as well as new homes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Remodels are one of our core services alongside new custom homes and ADUs.

faqs.question: Can we live in the house during the remodel?
Who handles structural work on an addition?
faqs.answer: We do. Foundations and framing are self-performed by our own concrete and framing crews.

title: ADUs
summary: Accessory dwelling units, built start to finish by the same team that builds our custom homes.
intro: An ADU is a small house with all the same systems as a large one. We build ADUs with the same crews and process we use on our custom homes: our own foundation, our own framing, and one point of contact from budget to move-in.

heroImage.alt: Placeholder standing in for a finished exterior photo of 4807 Seashore, Newport Beach

included.title: Budget and feasibility
included.body: An early look at what the lot and local rules allow, and what it will cost.

included.title: Plans and permitting support
included.body: We work with your designer and help carry the permit through plan check.

included.title: Foundation and framing
included.body: Poured and framed by our own crews.

included.title: Complete construction
included.body: Utilities, finishes and final inspection managed by one general contractor.

process.title: Budget
process.body: We review the lot and goals and build a working budget.

process.title: Design
process.body: We coordinate the design so it is buildable and fits the budget.

process.title: Permit
process.body: We help prepare the submittal and respond to plan-check comments.

process.title: Build
process.body: We build the ADU from foundation to final inspection.

faqs.question: Do you build detached and attached ADUs?
Do you help with permitting?
faqs.answer: Yes. Permitting is one of the four phases of our process, and we help prepare the submittal and respond to plan-check comments.

faqs.question: How much does an ADU cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on size, site and finishes. We price each project from quantity take-offs rather than a flat per-square-foot number.

title: Concrete & framing
summary: Structural concrete, rough framing and pre-fab framing by our own crews. The bones of every project we build.
intro: Most general contractors subcontract the structure. We pour and frame it ourselves. Structural concrete and rough framing are where a building's accuracy is set, and doing them in-house means the foundation, the frame and the schedule answer to the same people.

heroImage.alt: Placeholder standing in for a framing-stage jobsite photo of 4 Fairway Point, Newport Coast

included.title: Structural concrete
included.body: Footings, foundations, slabs and structural concrete for our own projects.

included.title: Rough framing
included.body: Wall, floor and roof framing by our own framing crew.

included.title: Pre-fab and modular framing
included.body: Panelized and modular framing where it saves time on site.

included.title: Lumber take-offs
included.body: Detailed lumber take-offs, also offered to builders and framers as a stand-alone service.

process.title: Take-off
process.body: We quantify concrete and lumber from the plans before anything is ordered.

process.title: Foundation
process.body: Our crew forms, reinforces and pours the footings and slab.

process.title: Frame
process.body: Our framers stand the structure, floor by floor, to the plans.

process.title: Hand-off
process.body: The frame is ready for the envelope and the rest of the trades, with no gap between subcontractors.

faqs.question: Do you subcontract your concrete or framing?
faqs.answer: No. Structural concrete and rough framing are self-performed by JM Kelley crews.

faqs.question: Do you offer concrete or framing on its own, for other builders?
Do you offer pre-fab or modular framing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Pre-fab and modular framing are part of our framing services.

faqs.question: Can I order a lumber take-off without hiring you to build?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our lumber take-off service has a 48-hour turnaround (some rules apply), priced on the complexity of the plans. See For Builders.

title: Owner's representation
summary: An experienced builder on your side of the table, wherever the project is.
intro: When you are building with another contractor, an owner's representative protects your interests: reviewing contracts, tracking the budget and making sure the work matches what you are paying for. We provide owner's representation and contract compliance, and we travel worldwide for clients.

heroImage.alt: Placeholder standing in for a finished exterior photo of 2000 East Oceanfront, Newport Beach

included.title: Contract compliance
included.body: We check the work, the schedule and the billing against the contract.

included.title: Bid and contract management
included.body: We help solicit, level and negotiate bids, and review contracts before you sign.

included.title: Budget compliance
included.body: We track spending against the budget and review change orders before they are approved.

included.title: Worldwide
included.body: We travel for clients, so the same representation is available beyond Orange County.

process.title: Review
process.body: We read the plans, the budget and any contracts already in place.

process.title: Plan
process.body: We agree with you on reporting, meeting cadence and what we approve on your behalf.

process.title: Represent
process.body: We attend meetings, review pay applications and change orders, and track the schedule.

process.title: Close out
process.body: We check completion, documentation and warranties before final payment.

faqs.question: Do you only represent owners in Orange County?
faqs.answer: No. We travel worldwide for owner's representation clients.

title: Project management
summary: Construction and project management from feasibility through job documentation.
intro: Construction and project management is the discipline that keeps a build on budget and on schedule. We manage the whole sequence, from the first feasibility questions to the last piece of job documentation.

heroImage.alt: Placeholder standing in for a finished exterior photo of 441, 443, 445 M Street, Newport Beach

included.title: Feasibility
included.body: What can be built, what it will cost, and what stands in the way.

included.title: Plan review
included.body: Constructability and cost review of drawings before pricing and permitting.

included.title: Bid and contract management
included.body: Bid packages, bid leveling and contracts for every trade.

included.title: Consultant management
included.body: Coordinating architects, engineers and consultants.

included.title: Budget compliance
included.body: Tracking every dollar against the approved budget.

included.title: Change orders
included.body: Priced, documented and approved before the work changes.

included.title: Value engineering
included.body: Finding cost savings that do not compromise the design intent.

included.title: Scheduling
included.body: A working schedule that is updated as the job moves.

included.title: Weekly meetings
included.body: A standing weekly meeting so decisions don't wait.

included.title: Job documentation
included.body: Photos, logs and records kept for the life of the project.

process.title: Budget
process.body: Feasibility and a working budget.

process.title: Design
process.body: Plan review, consultant management and value engineering.

process.title: Permit
process.body: Permit coordination and bid and contract management.

process.title: Build
process.body: Scheduling, weekly meetings, change orders and documentation.

faqs.question: Can you manage a project you are not building?
faqs.answer: Yes. Construction and project management, and owner's representation, are available as separate services.

faqs.question: How often will we meet?
faqs.answer: Weekly. Weekly meetings are part of how we manage every project.
